prompts.question: Explain how you would find the domain of (g/f).
prompts.answer: First, identify the domains of g and f. Then find the values that make (f(x)) equal zero and eliminate them from the domain.

prompts.question: Communicate Precisely How are the domains of (f+g), (f-g), (f· g), and (f/g) related to the domains of f and g?
prompts.answer: If f and g have the same domain, the domains of (f+g), (f-g), and (f· g) are that same domain. The domain of (f/g) is that same domain, but without any values for which g is zero. If f and g have different domains (as in Example 2), the domain for (f+g), (f-g), and (f· g) is the intersection of the two domains. The domain of (f/g) is further restricted by removing any values for which g is zero.
